items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And the man who sold me the drums, George Hamilton, he had a drum shop in Detroit.

ctx.x: And what kind of instrument was it?

It was a W.F.L, Ludwig’s. (W.F.L is the company started by William F Ludwig after the Great Depression in 1937. The company was simply W.F.L Drum Company until 1955 when it became known as Ludwig) That’s what they had. The band we had for Operation Happiness they had Slingerlands Drums, and they were some good drums as well. But Ludwig’s were in the range that I could handle, that I could pay as well. And the man who sold me the drums, George Hamilton, he had a drum shop in Detroit. His son runs it now. He played…
Did you get a 4-piece set? Do you remember what?
